items.summary: A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.

items.summary: TeamPass is a self-hosted collaborative password manager. Prior to 3.2.1.2, the update_folder action in app/sources/folders.queries.php allowed an authenticated, non-read-only user to re-parent a folder without checking whether the target folder or submitted parentId belonged to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. Selecting a personal folder as the new parent passed the personal-folder guard and set personal_folder on the target, transferring the credential subtree into the attacker's accessible space after the next login and hiding it from the organization, including administrators. The change exposed credential labels, logins, URLs, email addresses, and descriptions, while sharekey-protected passwords remained protected; hiding the subtree also denied other users access. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.1.2.

items.summary:
Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with ssl_session_cache 

shared:name:size

without an explicit ssl_session_ticket_key file directives to automatically rotate SSL session ticket keys, a remote unauthenticated attacker is able to forge client SSL sessions 

in a non-deterministic manner that is beyond the attacker's control. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to bypass verification of client certificates.

Impact


This vulnerability can lead to the exposure of resources or functionality to unintended actors, possibly providing attackers with access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

items.summary: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

items.summary:
FlowIntel contains an authorization flaw in its duplicate alert ingestion logic. When a duplicate alert is received and its content is updated, the ownership and visibility scope fields (owner user and owner organization) were not refreshed to reflect the connector's current scope. As a result, an alert that was originally created under a broader visibility scope retained that broader scope even after the connector's scope was narrowed or changed.

This means that users or organizations that should no longer have visibility into a given alert could continue to access it, because the stale ownership fields were never updated during the duplicate-update path. The issue affected all duplicate updates, including those involving alerts in terminal review states and those recovered from uniqueness conflicts.

Security impact:
- Unauthorized disclosure of security alert content to users or organizations outside the intended visibility scope.
- Stale access persists indefinitely until the alert is independently re-scoped or deleted.

Affected version: <4.1.0.

items.summary: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions 8.3.0 through 9.3.6, the internal helper that normalizes a path-scoped middleware's mount path only handles string inputs, but the use method also accepts an array of mount paths and passes it through unchanged, so the normalization silently does nothing. As a result, a trailing slash on an array element survives into the generated route-matching regular expression, and an element that is exactly the root path, meaning a catch-all mount, is dropped entirely. Requests to subroutes of the affected mount paths then skip the path-scoped middleware, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, while Fastify's router still dispatches them to the handler, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach protected routes. Applications are affected when they mount middleware on an array of paths in which an element ends with a slash, including one introduced by a plugin prefix that ends with a slash, or is exactly the root path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid array mount paths with a trailing slash element for security relevant middleware.

items.summary: @fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.

items.summary: A path traversal flaw was found in ansible-core. When installing a collection with ansible-galaxy collection install, the install destination directory is derived from the namespace and name fields declared inside the collection artifact's own metadata, which are not validated as well-formed collection identifiers or checked for path containment. A malicious collection artifact -- delivered as a local file, a remote URL, a source directory, a git repository, or as a dependency -- can use a crafted name value to redirect the install destination outside the configured collections path, causing ansible-galaxy to delete an existing directory writable by the invoking user and then write attacker-controlled files to that location.

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline appends each new block to a growing character buffer and reruns splitlines over the entire buffer on every iteration. An attacker-controlled corpus file containing one very long unterminated line therefore causes quadratic CPU consumption in line-oriented corpus readers and can deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

items.summary: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

items.summary:
The administration page "Offene
Bestellungen" (open orders) of the JTL PayPal Checkout plugin for JTL-Shop outputs the
customer name of pending orders without output encoding. A registered
customer (free self-registration) can submit an HTML-entity-encoded name, which is
decoded to markup when the billing address of an order is written. If
the PayPal payment is left unfinished, the order is listed on the page and the
name is rendered as markup in the browser of an administrator who opens
the page. The script code runs with the privileges of that administrator
and can, for example, create a new administrator account. Guest orders are
not affected, because the name is encoded again.

items.summary: Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Installation and Configuration).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology accessible data and unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle Hyperion Infrastructure Technology. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.2 (Confidentiality and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:L).

items.summary: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Hotspot).  Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u511b33-perf, 11.0.33.0.3, 17.0.21.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 27.0.1.0.3; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.21.0.3 and  21.0.13.0.3; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.20.0.3. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via multiple protocols to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition as well as  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data. Note: This vulnerability can be exploited by using APIs in the specified Component, e.g., through a web service which supplies data to the APIs. This vulnerability also applies to Java deployments, typically in clients running sandboxed Java Web Start applications or sandboxed Java applets, that load and run untrusted code (e.g., code that comes from the internet) and rely on the Java sandbox for security. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.5 (Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H).

items.summary: urllib3 is a user-friendly HTTP client library for Python. Starting in version 2.2.0 and prior to 2.5.0, urllib3 does not control redirects in browsers and Node.js. urllib3 supports being used in a Pyodide runtime utilizing the JavaScript Fetch API or falling back on XMLHttpRequest. This means Python libraries can be used to make HTTP requests from a browser or Node.js. Additionally, urllib3 provides a mechanism to control redirects, but the retries and redirect parameters are ignored with Pyodide; the runtime itself determines redirect behavior. This issue has been patched in version 2.5.0.

items.summary:
A NULL Pointer Dereference vulnerability in the Packet Forwarding Engine (pfe) of Juniper Networks Junos OS allows a local, low-privileged attacker to cause a Denial-of-Service (DoS).

When a specific command is executed, the pfe crashes. This will cause traffic forwarding to be interrupted until the system self-recovers. Repeated execution will create a sustained DoS condition.

 This issue only affects MX Series devices with Line cards MPC1-MPC9.
This issue affects:
Junos OS on MX Series: 


  *  All versions before 21.4R3-S9, 
  *  from 22.2 before 22.2R3-S5, 
  *  from 22.3 before 22.3R3-S4, 
  *  from 22.4 before 22.4R3-S2, 
  *  from 23.2 before 23.2R2-S1, 
  *  from 23.4 before 23.4R2.

items.summary:
An Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions vulnerability in packet processing of Juniper Networks Junos OS on MX Series with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 line cards, EX9200 with EX9200-15C lines cards, MX304 devices, and Juniper Networks Junos OS Evolved on PTX Series, allows an attacker sending malformed DHCP packets to cause ingress packet processing to stop, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS).  Continued receipt and processing of these packets will create a sustained Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

This issue only occurs if DHCP snooping is enabled. See configuration below.

This issue can be detected using following commands. Their output will display the interface status going down:


user@device>show interfaces <if--x/x/x>
user@device>show log messages | match <if--x/x/x>
user@device>show log messages ==> will display the "[Error] Wedge-Detect : Host Loopback Wedge Detected: PFE: no," logs.

This issue affects:
Junos OS on 

MX Series 

with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600 line cards, EX9200 with EX9200-15C line cards, and MX304: 


  *  All versions before 21.2R3-S7, 
  *  from 21.4 before 21.4R3-S6, 
  *  from 22.2 before 22.2R3-S3, 
  *  all versions of 22.3,
  *  from 22.4 before 22.4R3, 
  *  from 23.2 before 23.2R2; 



Junos OS Evolved on PTX Series: 
  *  from 19.3R1-EVO before 21.2R3-S8-EVO,

  *  from 21.4-EVO before 21.4R3-S7-EVO, 
  *  from 22.1-EVO before 22.1R3-S6-EVO, 
  *  from 22.2-EVO before 22.2R3-S5-EVO, 
  *  from 22.3-EVO before 22.3R3-S3-EVO, 
  *  from 22.4-EVO before 22.4R3-S1-EVO, 
  *  from 23.2-EVO before 23.2R2-S2-EVO, 
  *  from 23.4-EVO before 23.4R2-EVO.



Junos OS Evolved releases prior to 19.3R1-EVO are unaffected by this vulnerability

items.summary: A command injection flaw was found in rpm. Installing or rebuilding a source RPM whose source or spec file basenames contain a %() macro construct causes rpm to execute an attacker-controlled shell command via popen() while relocating the source file list. This allows arbitrary command execution as the invoking (typically non-root) user, simply by installing, rebuilding, or otherwise processing an untrusted .src.rpm.

items.summary: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. Parsing a symlink entry in an untrusted RPM package whose declared RPMTAG_LONGFILESIZES value is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF causes an integer overflow in iterReadArchiveNext() that shrinks a buffer allocation to one byte, after which the payload's independently-controlled cpio filesize field is used to write attacker-controlled data past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an  untrusted package.

MRemoteNG uses single MD5 hash with no salt and no iterations for key-derivation. An attacker who obtains the encrypted data can brute-force
a weak or moderate passphrase offline at extreme speed and then decrypt every stored connection
password. When the default passphrase is in use, no cracking is needed at all; the key is derived from a
publicly known value.


Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

MRemoteNG establishes encrypted but unauthenticated channel with Microsoft SQL Server backend. Client accepts any certificate the server
presents, including a self-signed certificate supplied by an attacker. An attacker positioned between the client and the SQL server (for example via ARP/DNS spoofing) can
transparently pintercept the connection (man-in-the-middle) and read all traffic, including the encrypted connection-password table read and the database login.




Vendor did not provide the range of vulnerable versions. Only version 1.76.20 was tested and confirmed vulnerable. Other versions may also be vulnerable.

items.summary: The WP Duplicate – WordPress Migration Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in versions up to, and including, 1.1.11. This is due to a missing capability check and missing nonce check on the start_zip_creation, start_zip_download, local_sync_get_init_root_files, and local_sync_get_files_by_key AJAX actions in the start_zip_creation_dev() and sibling functions. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite the plugin's prod_site_url setting so it points at an attacker-controlled host and enumerate arbitrary server directories, which when combined with a subsequent administrator-triggered sync results in an unsigned attacker-supplied ZIP archive being fetched, extracted via a WordPress-independent bridge deployed under the web root, resulting in remote code execution on the affected site.

items.summary: Aperi'Solve is an open-source steganalysis web platform. Prior to 3.4.2, an unauthenticated user can submit a PNG to POST /upload, which reaches aperisolve/utils/png.py through analyze_image, PCRTAnalyzer, PNG.repair(), and check_idat(). A malformed IDAT chunk can make attacker-controlled length and newline data drive an unbounded combinations search in PNG._fix_dos2unix(), causing repeated CRC checks that occupy a worker and delay or block image analysis for other users. Per-IP upload limits and eventual job termination bound the denial of service, and the issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.4.2.

items.summary: django-docutils provides reStructuredText support for Django. Prior to 0.30.0, public rendering paths including publish_doctree, publish_html_from_source, publish_html_from_doctree, publish_parts_from_doctree, the {% rst %} template tag, the rst template filter, DocutilsTemplates, and DocutilsView pass lower-trust reStructuredText to Docutils without disabling file_insertion_enabled, raw_enabled, ambient docutils.conf processing, or unsafe URI schemes and without consistently sanitizing doctrees. An attacker who can influence rendered reStructuredText can use include or csv-table directives to read local files or cause server-side URL requests, or use raw HTML and unsafe URI output to inject stored script-capable content. Applications that render only trusted static reStructuredText are not affected unless attackers can influence it. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP UpdateFirmware requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29487.

items.summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). From 0.29.13 until 0.31.0, the Docker terminal, container-log, and monitoring WebSocket handlers accept a caller-controlled serviceId as authorization but do not consistently bind the requested containerId or appName to that service. A member with read access to any service can consequently target unrelated containers, obtain a root shell in the Dokploy panel container, read other tenants' logs and statistics, and use the mounted Docker socket to compromise the host. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

items.summary:
An incorrect
permission assignment vulnerability in Omada SDN Controller prior to 6.2.20 may
cause a database backup generated during the uninstall workflow to remain
readable by other local users on the host. 





Successful
exploitation requires local, low-privileged access to the affected host and a

items.summary:
The Strava datasource plugin's resource handler POST /strava-api forwards a client-supplied endpoint string, and its query parameters, to the Strava API (https://www.strava.com/api/v3/<endpoint>) without validation.

When the datasource is not in OAuth pass-through mode, the request is made with the access token stored on the datasource, not the caller's identity. Grafana authorises plugin resource calls only on the datasources:query permission, which Viewers have by default. Any such caller could therefore request any Strava API path the connected account's OAuth grant allows, for example athlete/clubs or routes/{id}, and read the response.

The plugin's frontend (stravaApi.ts) only needs a fixed set of paths: athlete, athlete/activities, activities/{id}, activities/{id}/streams and segments/{id}.

Requests to Strava are GET only, so the issue is read-only.

Affected: plugin versions 1.2.0 through 1.7.2. The fix restricts endpoint to those five patterns and is pending release. The check runs before the access token is resolved, so a rejected request never causes a token refresh or any call to Strava. Paths with .. segments are rejected as well.

items.summary:
In Eclipse iceoryx-rs, versions 0.0.11 to 0.0.13 and 0.1.0 as well as on the latest main branch.



`SampleReceiver::<T>::take()` and `Sample::<T>::deref()` are safe functions that hand the caller a `&T` pointing at a chunk written by another iceoryx process, but the subscriber path neither requires `T: ShmSend` nor verifies that the received chunk is at least `size_of::<T>()` bytes / `align_of::<T>()`-aligned. A peer process that publishes an undersized chunk, or any chunk at all when the subscriber chose a pointer-bearing `T`, drives a `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` subscriber into out-of-bounds reads of adjacent shared-memory chunks or dereference of a publisher-controlled pointer.



Resolution:



It will not be fixed since this is a known limitation in iceoryx as it is the users responsibility to specify the same data type on sender and receiver side.



[iceoryx2](https://github.com/eclipse-iceoryx/iceoryx2) is the successor of iceoryx-rs where the API is designed to prevent this by default.



It is strongly recommended to migrate to iceoryx2 which is actively maintained and receives security support.



The iceoryx-rs package has officially reached End-of-life and will not receive any features, bugfixes or security fixes.

Prior to 0.8.1, src/trust/ChainBuilder.ts ChainBuilder.tryBuild() terminates chain construction when an attacker-controlled certificate Subject Distinguished Name equals a trusted anchor subject, without verifying cryptographic closure to the anchor public key. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply a self-signed leaf or intermediate that reuses the trusted Subject Distinguished Name and have credentials signed by the attacker key accepted as issued by the trusted authority. The public src/trust/TrustEvaluator.ts TrustEvaluator.evaluate() path compounds the error by matching a terminus through serialNumber and falling back to anchors[0], which can attribute the forged chain to genuine trusted-authority metadata. An MCP caller with tool-session access can therefore use domshell_eval to mutate DOM, window, or global state while the host approval interface, server authorization flags, denial messages, and audit records represent the operation as read-only. The bypass does not expose a capability beyond domshell_js for callers already authorized to write, but it violates the configured permission boundary for callers lacking that authorization. From 3000.0.0 until 3000.18.1, OliveTin passes attacker-influenceable output and ot_username values into shellAfterCompleted processing in service/internal/executor/executor.go without applying checkShellArgumentSafety, the shell-safety validation used for primary action execution. The same post-execution template path also expands exitCode without that validation, but the advisory does not establish attacker control of the exit-code value. When an action configures shellAfterCompleted with output or ot_username, shell metacharacters from command output, external data processed by an action, or a trusted-header username can become syntax in the command executed by the stepExecAfter path. This can execute arbitrary commands as the OliveTin process user, including when the primary action uses the safer exec-array mode. This issue is fixed in version 3000.18.1.

items.summary: AnsibleForms is a self-hosted web application that turns automation into self-service forms. Prior to 6.2.1, AnsibleForms allows a user with repository management privileges to inject shell syntax through repository uri, branch, name, or host values processed by server/src/models/repo.model.js. The Repo.clone and Repo.addKnownHosts paths interpolate these values into git and ssh-keyscan command strings, and server/src/lib/cmd.js executes the strings through Cmd.executeSilentCommand with shell interpretation enabled. Creating or updating a repository can therefore execute arbitrary commands as the AnsibleForms application process. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.1.

items.summary: ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when a challenge payload omits the signature field, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker can remove the signature, supply attacker-selected low-difficulty challenge parameters, solve the resulting proof of work, and submit a payload that verifies successfully, bypassing the CAPTCHA control. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

items.summary: djangocms-moderation provides an approval workflow mechanism for organizations that require content approval before publication. Prior to 2.4.0, CollectionCommentAdmin and RequestCommentAdmin in the Django admin use changelist_view and changeform_view to scope comment access through caller-controlled object identifiers and model-level view_collectioncomment or view_requestcomment permissions without invoking ModerationRequest.user_can_view_comments() or an equivalent collection participant check. An authenticated staff user with either view permission can enumerate collection or moderation-request identifiers and read full comment messages for workflows they do not participate in. The exposure affects confidentiality of internal editorial discussions; comment creation, modification, and deletion remain protected, and integrity and availability are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.0.

items.summary: django-filer is a file and image management application for Django. Prior to 3.5.0, the delete_files_or_folders action in filer/admin/folderadmin.py checks global Django model-level deletion permission but omits check_folder_edit_permissions and check_files_edit_permissions when FILER_ENABLE_PERMISSIONS is enabled. An authenticated staff user who has a global delete_file, delete_folder, or delete_image permission but is limited to read-only access by FolderPermission can therefore delete files, folders, and descendants from the restricted folder. Deployments using the default disabled per-folder permission system are not affected, and the issue does not create a read-confidentiality impact. This issue is fixed in version 3.5.0.

items.summary: LLMKube is a Kubernetes operator for self-hosted large language model inference across heterogeneous hardware. Prior to 0.9.0, the ModelReconciler accepts arbitrary absolute paths and file:// URIs in Model.spec.source without restricting them to approved roots. A namespace user who can create or update Model and InferenceService resources can cause copyLocalModel to open an attacker-selected file in the controller pod or cause a HostPathVolumeSource to mount an attacker-selected node file when modelCache.enabled is enabled, which is the default. The selected file is copied into model storage and can expose controller service-account credentials or other node secrets outside the attacker's namespace. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

items.summary: Jane is a set of PHP libraries that generates models and API clients from JSON Schema and OpenAPI specifications. Prior to 7.12.0, Jane's Reference.php::doResolve passes an attacker-controlled OpenAPI $ref target to file_get_contents without restricting its scheme or resolved local path. When a victim generates code from an attacker-influenced document, an HTTP or HTTPS reference can cause requests to attacker-chosen or internal services, while an absolute or parent-relative path can read local JSON or YAML files and inline the retrieved content into generated output. Exploitation occurs during generation or CI processing and can disclose local files and internal-service responses. This issue is fixed in version 7.12.0.

A header parameter name containing a PHPDoc closing delimiter can terminate the comment early and place attacker-controlled PHP in class-body position, including an __construct method that runs when the generated Client is instantiated. Exploitation requires generating a client from an attacker-influenced OpenAPI document and then using the generated SDK, and can execute arbitrary PHP with the consuming application's privileges. items.summary: Gortex is a high-performance code-intelligence engine for AI agents and integrated development environments. Prior to 0.55.0, resolveFilePath in internal/mcp/tools_fileops.go accepts absolute paths without checking indexed repository roots, while write_file, edit_file, and move_inline in internal/mcp/tools_move_inline.go omit guardSymlinkWithinRepo before reaching AtomicWriteFile and related write sinks. A caller that can influence MCP tool arguments can therefore create or overwrite files anywhere the daemon user can access, including startup or hook files that execute code on a later trigger. The flaw violates Gortex's repository-confinement invariant and can lead to arbitrary host code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.55.0.

items.summary: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4, HashChainVerifier in the common-message module resolves attacker-controlled batch-signature hash chains before verifying the message signature and signing certificate, without cycle detection, recursion-depth or total-step limits, or per-step memoization. A registered ecosystem member can send a small crafted hashchain MIME part with repeated or cyclic StepRef values so that verifyHashChain() performs exponential work or unbounded recursion before authentication. Repeated requests can exhaust Security Server proxy threads and deny data-exchange service, and a self-reference can raise an uncaught error. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4.

items.summary: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. Prior to 2.5, the filename parameter accepted by POST /qsl/addQsoToQsl in application/controllers/Qsl.php addQsoToQsl() is stored without rejecting directory separators or relative path components, and POST /qsl/delete reaches application/models/Qsl_model.php deleteQsl(), which passes the planted qsl_images filename to unlink(). A standard authenticated user can associate the malicious filename with the user's own QSO, satisfy the ownership check, escape the per-user QSL image directory, and delete files writable by the PHP worker. Deleting configuration or operational files can cause denial of service, while deleting installer gate files can reopen the unauthenticated installer and enable application identity takeover through attacker-controlled database configuration. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.

items.summary: Open OnDemand is an open-source high-performance computing portal. Prior to 4.1.6 and 4.2.3, apps/dashboard/config/initializers/session_store.rb stores dashboard sessions by default in a predictable /var/tmp/<username> directory, or in another location configured by an administrator, but omits PUN user directory ownership and mode 0700 validation. A local attacker can pre-create another user's directory, read the victim's session identifier and CSRF token after login, or stage a predetermined session identifier. ActiveSupport file-store deserialization of attacker-controlled cache data may also occur in the victim's context, enabling file modification or code execution with the victim's privileges. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.6 and 4.2.3.

items.summary: In Eclipse Yasson versions 3.0 to 3.0.5, a race condition (CWE-362) exists in the handling of @JsonbNumberFormat. Yasson creates one java.text.NumberFormat instance per annotated property and shares it across all threads that use the same Jsonb instance. NumberFormat is not thread-safe, and the deserializer called parse() on it without synchronization. When multiple threads deserialize concurrently, a thread can receive a numeric value that belongs to another thread's input, receive an incorrect value, or fail with an exception. A remote attacker who can send concurrent requests to an application that deserializes untrusted JSON this way may cause incorrect data to be processed or cause another user's value to be returned. Exploitation requires that the application use @JsonbNumberFormat with a shared Jsonb instance and that the attacker win a timing race. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.6 by synchronizing access to the shared NumberFormat instances.

items.summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.0, failed Railpack builds and database backups propagate an execution error containing the full command, exposing application environment variables, database passwords, and S3 access keys embedded in those commands. When the corresponding App Build Error or Database Backup notification setting is enabled, the disclosure can send secrets to email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, or webhooks; the same secrets are written separately to persistent Dokploy container logs, which may be accessible to more principals than the affected service. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.

items.summary: The Fancy Lightbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation without administrator interaction requires that the attacker first have one comment approved so that a subsequent payload comment is auto-published; the injected script only executes when a user clicks the malicious image link inside the comment. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

items.summary: The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core comment KSES permits unauthenticated commenters to post anchor elements with href and title attributes, so an entity-encoded payload stored in the title attribute survives sanitization verbatim; the browser then decodes the entities when populating the DOM .title property, and the Slimbox library's jQuery .html() caption sink renders it as executable HTML.

KiCad Altium SCHLIB File Parsing Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of KiCad. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of SCHLIB files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated object. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-33213.

items.summary: The AIKTP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authorization Bypass via Predictable Token in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.7. The vulnerability exists because the plugin's sync token (`aiktpz_token`) is generated using PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid()` function — producing a wall-clock-derived value with approximately one million microsecond candidates per uncertain generation second — while the unauthenticated, unthrottled REST endpoint `/wp-json/aiktp/checkToken` (registered with `permission_callback => __return_true`) acts as a public brute-force oracle for the token; simultaneously, the capability checks in `check_valid_token` and its wrappers (`verify_aiktp_token_with_edit_capability`, `verify_aiktp_token_with_upload_capability`) inspect only a server-side stored Administrator account (option `aiktp_author`) rather than the actual REST caller, meaning possession of the token alone grants Administrator-equivalent authority to any external request. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to recover the sync token and then invoke `POST /wp-json/aiktp/createpost` to publish arbitrary posts attributed to a site Administrator, `POST /wp-json/aiktp/doUpdatePostWithImageURL` to overwrite the body content of any existing post, and `POST /wp-json/aiktp/doUploadImageToWP` to import remote media and attach it as the featured image of any post. Additionally, when the `aiktpz_token` option has never been initialized, the `checkToken` oracle returns success for an empty token submission due to a loose comparison in `check_valid_token`, providing a zero-effort bypass that requires no brute-forcing whatsoever.

items.summary: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU

The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before
the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU
can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined
SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter
SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer.

An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE
that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection
is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU.
This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without
changing when need_neg is cleared.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: don't wait for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync()

smbdirect_socket_destroy_sync() waited for RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED
after smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work() called rdma_disconnect(). That
can take very long, e.g. if the peer just disappeared, until the
rdma cm gives up, or forever if the event already happened, but the
status was overwritten afterwards.

This is not needed: smbdirect_socket_destroy() drains the qp under
rdma_lock_handler(), destroys it and calls rdma_destroy_id(), which
only waits for a currently running event handler and makes sure no
further events are delivered. The rest of the disconnect protocol
(DREQ/DREP and timewait for IB, abrupt close for iWarp) is handled
by the rdma core asynchronously. drivers/nvme/host/rdma.c also just
calls rdma_disconnect() and ib_drain_qp() before rdma_destroy_id().

So smbdirect_socket_destroy() now also accepts
SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTING and changes the status to
SMBDIRECT_SOCKET_DISCONNECTED itself under rdma_lock_handler().

We could still get RDMA_CM_EVENT_DISCONNECTED in the small
windows between rdma_unlock_handler() and rdma_destroy_id(),
but in that case smbdirect_connection_rdma_event_handler()
is basically a no-op.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: release failed pending sockets of a listener

A child of a listener only left the listen.pending or listen.ready
list via smbdirect_socket_accept() or when the listener was
destroyed. So every connection that failed before it was accepted
(negotiate timeout, peer disconnect, invalid negotiate request, ...)
stayed on the list and counted against the backlog until the listener
was destroyed. After about backlog (10 for ksmbd) such connections
smbdirect_listen_connect_request() rejected every new connection with
-EBUSY, so an unauthenticated peer was able to permanently stop
ksmbd from accepting SMB-Direct connections.

Now a failed child moves itself to a new listen.orphaned list at the
end of smbdirect_socket_cleanup_work(), after the disconnect was
started, and queues listen.purge_orphaned_work, which releases it
with smbdirect_socket_release(), without holding the listener's
rdma_lock_handler() lock, in the same way smbdirect_socket_destroy()
does for the remaining children. Orphaned sockets still count against
the backlog until they are released.

sc->accept.listener is now only changed under listener->listen.lock
and whoever clears it is responsible for releasing the socket:
smbdirect_socket_accept(), purge_orphaned_work or the destroy of the
listener.

In order to make that work:

- a struct smbdirect_socket that is a listener is now freed via
  kfree_rcu(), so that a child can dereference sc->accept.listener
  under rcu_read_lock(), even if the listener is released concurrently.

- smbdirect_listen_connect_request() adds nsc to the listen.pending
  list and sets nsc->accept.listener before it calls
  smbdirect_accept_connect_request(), and always returns 0 so the
  rdma_cm core keeps the connection id and nsc owns it. On a non-zero
  return it schedules nsc's teardown with
  smbdirect_socket_schedule_cleanup(), which orphans it off the
  listener so that purge_orphaned_work releases it; nsc destroys its
  own connection id with rdma_destroy_id() in that teardown. The
  teardown has to be deferred because the rdma_cm core holds nsc's
  id_priv->handler_mutex across the handler, so nsc->rdma.cm_id must
  not be destroyed synchronously from here. That same handler_mutex
  (and the listener's) also guarantees nsc can't go away under us,
  so setting the listener before the call is safe and lets a failure
  orphan nsc.

- smbdirect_accept_negotiate_recv_work() no longer moves a socket to
  the ready list if it already failed or no longer belongs to the
  listener. Every accepting socket has a listener, so if
  sc->accept.listener is already cleared, it no longer sends a
  negotiate response, as the socket is about to be released.

- smbdirect_socket_destroy() of the listener disables
  purge_orphaned_work and also releases the orphaned sockets.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: reject FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on a directory handle

An authenticated client with a writable tree connection can open a
directory with FILE_WRITE_DATA and send FSCTL_SET_ZERO_DATA on that
handle. The handler only checks fp->daccess & FILE_WRITE_DATA_LE, but on
a directory FILE_WRITE_DATA is the legitimate add-file right, so the
check passes. ksmbd_vfs_zero_data() then calls kernel_write() on the
directory file, which has no FMODE_WRITE, and __kernel_write_iter()
hits WARN_ON_ONCE(!(file->f_mode & FMODE_WRITE)), panicking a
panic_on_warn kernel.

Before commit 25e414db7033 ("ksmbd: report holes in allocated range
queries") the dense-file path used vfs_fallocate(), which rejects
directories with -EISDIR. The kernel_write() loop that replaced it has
no such check. Reject a directory handle in ksmbd_vfs_zero_data() before
writing, as ksmbd_vfs_write() already does for SMB2_WRITE.

  WARNING: fs/read_write.c:608 at __kernel_write_iter+0x74b/0x8c0
  Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
  Call Trace:
   kernel_write+0x1ef/0x4d0
   ksmbd_vfs_zero_data+0x413/0x590
   smb2_ioctl+0x21fa/0x66a0
   handle_ksmbd_work+0x61b/0x1ff0

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fork: don't create io threads once PF_POSTCOREDUMP is set

zap_process() skips every thread that already has PF_POSTCOREDUMP set.
Such a thread is past synchronize_group_exit(), so a coredump can't
catch it anymore. It isn't counted in core_state->threads_remaining and
it isn't sent SIGKILL.

do_exit() sets PF_POSTCOREDUMP in synchronize_group_exit() and calls
io_uring_files_cancel() right after that. The cancellation runs task
work and a create_worker_cb() that io-wq queued before the exit creates
a new io-wq worker from there. If another thread started a coredump in
the meantime that worker joins a thread-group which is already being
dumped. zap_process() never saw it so it was never counted. But when it
exits it sees signal->core_state in synchronize_group_exit() and
decrements threads_remaining like any other thread.

So the count reaches zero one thread early and the dumper leaves
coredump_wait_inactive() while a thread it counted is still running.

The task has no fatal signal pending because zap_process() deliberately
didn't send it one, and it never went through get_signal() so it doesn't
have PF_SIGNALED either.

Refuse to create an io thread when the creator has PF_POSTCOREDUMP.
That costs nothing. io_uring_files_cancel() raises IO_WQ_BIT_EXIT
before it runs any task work, so a worker created from there only ever
gets to exit again, and io_should_retry_thread() doesn't retry -EINTR.

Clearing PF_POSTCOREDUMP for the new thread in copy_process() was the
other option. It makes the worker a thread like any other, but it only
helps while the dump hasn't started. A worker born after zap_process()
has run is invisible to it whatever its flags say and still decrements
threads_remaining on the way out. Refusing to create it covers both, and
then no task is ever born with the flag, so there is nothing to clear.

Moving io_uring_files_cancel() ahead of synchronize_group_exit() closes
the same window. It runs the cancellation, and whatever that can block
on, before the thread announces itself to the dumper. A thread that
blocks there never reaches coredump_task_exit() at all, so the dumper
ends up waiting for a thread that never parks. Refusing the creation
leaves the cancellation where it is. But it's very ugly to run io_uring
work even before we did all the generic exit work.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mt76: mt7925: fix reset panic caused by the WM2 rx irq mask

mt7925_irq_map sets wm2_complete_mask, but mt7925_dma_layout has no
tx done ring, so the MT_RXQ_MCU_WA queue and its NAPI are never set up.
On a chip reset, mt7925e_mac_reset() calls napi_disable() on that NAPI
and crashes:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000a40
  Workqueue: mt76 mt7925_mac_reset_work [mt7925_common]
  RIP: 0010:mutex_lock+0x1c/0x50
  Call Trace:
   napi_disable+0x1d/0x50
   mt7925e_mac_reset+0x327/0x420 [mt7925e]
   mt7925_mac_reset_work+0x9a/0x1a0 [mt7925_common]

Remove the WM2 mask from mt7925_irq_map and from
MT7925_INT_RX_DONE_ALL.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ARM: 9524/1: mm: align hugetlb mappings to the huge page size

mmap(MAP_HUGETLB) on 32-bit Arm can return an address which is not
aligned to the huge page size. In a QEMU virt guest, unmapping the VMA
then hits the alignment check in __unmap_hugepage_range():

  kernel BUG at mm/hugetlb.c:5213!
  Internal error: Oops - BUG: 0 [#1] SMP ARM
  PC is at __unmap_hugepage_range+0x540/0x584
  LR is at __zap_vma_range+0x13a0/0x1410

Commit 7bd3f1e1a9ae ("mm: make hugetlb mappings go through
mm_get_unmapped_area_vmflags") made hugetlb mappings use the
architecture's arch_get_unmapped_area(). The generic implementations
handle hugetlb alignment, but the Arm implementations only account for
the optional SHMLBA cache-colouring constraint. A 4 KiB-page kernel can
therefore align the mapping to 4 KiB or 16 KiB instead of the required
2 MiB.

Set the alignment mask from the file's hstate for hugetlb mappings in
both Arm implementations. Huge-page alignment also satisfies the
SHMLBA constraint.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

blk-crypto: fix NULL deref and UAF in __blk_crypto_evict_key()

Sashiko reported a possible NULL pointer dereference, triggered by the
following flow:

  dm-inlinecrypt ctor            # first use of the fallback
   ├─ blk_crypto_init_key()      # succeeds, ctx->key.size != 0
   ├─ blk_crypto_start_using_key()
   │   ├─ hw-wrapped key: -EOPNOTSUPP
   │   │    # profile never allocated (NULL)
   │   └─ raw key: fallback_start_using_mode()
   │      └─ blk_crypto_fallback_init() fails
   │         └─ kfree(profile)   # not NULLed
   ├─ goto bad
   └─ inlinecrypt_dtr()          # evicts whenever key.size is set
      └─ blk_crypto_evict_key()
         └─ blk_crypto_config_supported_natively() = false
            └─ blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key()
               └─ __blk_crypto_evict_key(blk_crypto_fallback_profile)
                  └─ profile->num_slots # BOOM!!!

This issue can be reproduced using the following commands:

  dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/backing bs=1M count=64
  LOOP=$(losetup -f --show /tmp/backing)
  SZ=$(blockdev --getsz $LOOP)
  KEY=$(head -c 64 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
  dmsetup create ic --table "0 $SZ inlinecrypt aes-xts-plain64 \
    $KEY 0 $LOOP 0 1 keytype:hw-wrapped"

And the following oops is triggered:

  ==================================================================
  blk-crypto: loop0: no support for wrapped keys
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
        0xdffffc000000000b: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN PTI
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000058-0x000000000000005f]
  CPU: 5 UID: 0 PID: 901 Comm: dmsetup 7.3.0-rc3 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  RIP: 0010:__blk_crypto_evict_key+0x2e/0x3b0
  Call Trace:
   blk_crypto_evict_key+0x24c/0x320
   inlinecrypt_dtr+0xf6/0x160
   inlinecrypt_ctr+0x2d3/0xbd0
   dm_table_add_target+0x661/0xf40
   table_load+0x1c4/0x490
   ctl_ioctl+0x32f/0x5f0
   dm_ctl_ioctl+0xe/0x20
  ==================================================================

dm-inlinecrypt is the only caller that can evict a key that was never
started, as fscrypt frees such a key without evicting it.

Fix this by returning early from blk_crypto_fallback_evict_key() when
tfms_inited[] is not set for the key's mode.  tfms_inited[] is only set
after blk_crypto_fallback_init() has successfully initialized the
profile, so the crash above is no longer reachable.

The bug has been latent since commit c984ff1423ae ("blk-crypto:
dynamically allocate fallback profile") was merged in v6.5, and only
became actually triggerable when commit e7f57d2c47e2 ("dm-inlinecrypt:
add target for inline block device encryption") was merged in v7.2.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag

A ceph mount oopses in ceph_readdir() when the MDS answers a READDIR
request with a reply whose extra blob is empty.  parse_reply_info()
skips reply blobs whose length is zero, so parse_reply_info_readdir()
never runs, r_reply_info.dir_dir stays NULL, and the reply still
parses as successful.  ceph_mdsc_do_request() returns 0 and
ceph_readdir() then reads rinfo->dir_dir->frag with no NULL check:

	/* extra */
	ceph_decode_32_safe(&p, end, len, bad);
	if (len > 0) {
		...
		err = parse_reply_info_extra(&p, p + len, req, features, s);
		...
	}

The oops on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820, one getdents64(2) on the
mount root after an ms_mode=legacy mount, trimmed:

BUG: KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000000-0x0000000000000007]
Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xdffffc0000000000: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 266 Comm: ls Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:ceph_readdir+0xbff/0x3ea0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 ? __pfx_ceph_readdir+0x10/0x10
 wrap_directory_iterator+0xa2/0xe0
 iterate_dir+0x1da/0x5d0
 __x64_sys_getdents64+0x13b/0x2a0
 do_syscall_64+0xdd/0x4a0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 </TASK>

The unconditional frag read came in with 81c6aea5275ea ("ceph: handle
frag mismatch between readdir request and reply"), so the bug is old.

Treat a reply with no dirfrag as a protocol violation: warn once,
drop the request and return -EIO, the same way ceph_readdir() already
handles the two malformed-reply cases later in the function.

Tested on v7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 (KASAN).  Unpatched, the
getdents64(2) above takes the machine down (oops=panic) on the first
READDIR reply.  With the patch it warns once and getdents64(2)
returns -EIO, no oops, no hang.  A conformant reply for an empty
directory — dirfrag present, zero entries, FRAG_END|FRAG_COMPLETE —
still lists "." and ".." and returns EOF on both kernels, so normal
readdir behavior is unchanged.  The oops is still present in
v7.3-rc5 (72d3fcf802c45).

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: serialize directory emptiness checks with readdir

SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY holds fp->readdir_lock while it calls iterate_dir()
on fp->filp. An SMB2 SET_INFO request with FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION
can resolve the same FileId and call ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir() on the same
filp without that lock.

iterate_dir()'s inode read lock permits concurrent readers and does not
serialize per-file iterator state. ext4 stores its dx readdir cursor and
fname RB tree in file->private_data. Concurrent reset or refill can
therefore free a fname node while the other worker still traverses it or
retains its RB-tree link, resulting in use-after-free accesses.

An authenticated SMB client with list and delete rights on a directory in
a writable KSMBD share backed by ext4 can trigger this when the directory
takes the dx readdir path. The client overlaps an SMB2 QUERY_DIRECTORY
request with an SMB2 SET_INFO request carrying FILE_DISPOSITION_INFORMATION
on one live FileId.

In one x86_64 SMP KASAN multi-shot guest using ksmbd-for-next at
171df27077fb, the unmodified kernel reported a cross-worker use-after-free
before a panic. The first report's access and free stacks show the two
request paths directly (trimmed):

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550
  Read of size 8 by task kworker/2:0/29
  Workqueue: ksmbd-io handle_ksmbd_work
  Call Trace:
   ext4_htree_store_dirent+0x488/0x550
   htree_dirblock_to_tree+0x535/0x990
   ext4_htree_fill_tree+0x319/0xba0
   ext4_readdir+0x175a/0x2f40
   iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630
   smb2_query_dir+0x1003/0x1cc0

  Freed by task 279:
   free_rb_tree_fname+0x67/0xc0
   ext4_readdir+0x13a9/0x2f40
   iterate_dir+0x1b6/0x630
   ksmbd_vfs_empty_dir+0xa2/0x100
   smb2_set_info+0x2ffa/0x45d0

Take fp->readdir_lock across the entire emptiness check. This places both
iterators over that handle's filp in the same lock domain while
preserving the disposition status handling. The exact code change
completed a warning-free x86_64 KASAN bzImage build. Tracing three request
pairs showed that the two iterate_dir() calls no longer overlapped and the
expected statuses were preserved. A further 1,600 reproducer iterations
completed with expected statuses and no KASAN report, Oops, or panic.

The reproducer and complete guest configuration are available privately
to maintainers on request.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: usbtv: fix null-pointer dereference on disconnect

A null-pointer dereference can occur in usb_make_path() when called from
usbtv_querycap() (and other ioctl handlers) during device disconnection.

Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
0xdffffc000000000a: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x0000000000000050-0x0000000000000057]
RIP: 0010:usb_make_path include/linux/usb.h:985 [inline]
RIP: 0010:usbtv_querycap+0x9c/0x100
drivers/media/usb/usbtv/usbtv-video.c:612
...
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 v4l_querycap+0x236/0x470 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:1106
 __video_do_ioctl+0x8af/0xc70 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3133
 video_usercopy+0x860/0x1430 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c:3475
 v4l2_ioctl+0x18d/0x1e0 drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-dev.c:366
 vfs_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:51 [inline]
 __do_sys_ioctl fs/ioctl.c:597 [inline]
 __se_sys_ioctl+0xfc/0x170 fs/ioctl.c:583
 do_syscall_x64 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63 [inline]
 do_syscall_64+0x174/0x580 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94

This happens due to a race condition between the USB device disconnect
routine (usbtv_disconnect()) and V4L2 ioctls. When the device is
disconnected, usbtv_disconnect() sets usbtv->udev = NULL without holding
the usbtv->v4l2_lock mutex. Concurrently, an ioctl handler like
usbtv_querycap() can be executing under the v4l2_lock and attempt to use
usbtv->udev, leading to a crash.

To fix this, move the usbtv->udev = NULL assignment into usbtv_video_free()
and protect it with mutex_lock(&usbtv->v4l2_lock). This ensures that no
non-queue ioctl handler can run concurrently with the pointer being
nullified. If an ioctl is already running, the mutex will block the
disconnect path until the ioctl finishes. If an ioctl is blocked waiting
for the lock, it will acquire it after the disconnect routine releases it,
but will then check video_is_registered() (which was cleared by
vb2_video_unregister_device()) and safely return -ENODEV.

Acquiring v4l2_lock after vb2_video_unregister_device() avoids
reintroducing a historical deadlock issue, and usbtv_audio_free() remains
safe as it is called before usbtv_video_free().

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: usb: pegasus: do not advance rx_skb->data on dropped frames

For the 0x8513 chip, read_bulk_callback() skips the 2-byte receive
header by advancing pegasus->rx_skb->data in place. This is done before
the pkt_len > PEGASUS_MTU check, and when that check drops the frame
the good path resubmits the same skb with the advanced rx_skb->data as
the transfer buffer, still PEGASUS_MTU bytes long.

Every frame with an oversized length field therefore moves the receive
buffer two more bytes towards the end of the skb data area. A device
that keeps sending such frames makes the host controller write received
data over skb_shared_info and past the end of the allocation, and the
corrupted skb_shared_info is used when the skb is eventually freed.
With an emulated device sending frames filled with 0x5a on a KASAN
kernel:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in dummy_timer+0xade/0x3f00 [dummy_hcd]
  Write of size 1536 at addr ffff888105821202 by task swapper/1/0
  ...
  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address 0xeb4b474b4b4b4b4c: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP KASAN NOPTI
  KASAN: maybe wild-memory-access in range [0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a60-0x5a5a5a5a5a5a5a67]
  RIP: 0010:skb_release_data+0x36f/0x800

Only skip the header with skb_reserve() once the frame is going to be
passed up, so the receive buffer always starts at the beginning of the
skb data area. Unlike the old pointer adjustment, skb_reserve() also
moves skb->tail, so the two header bytes now count against the buffer
size: lower the length limit for the 0x8513 accordingly, otherwise a
pkt_len of PEGASUS_MTU - 1 or PEGASUS_MTU would trip skb_over_panic().

Found by code review with LLM assistance and reproduced with an
emulated USB device (raw-gadget + dummy_hcd).

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: fix race between client_info_show() and free_client()

client_info_show() renders /proc/fs/nfsd/clients/<id>/info and walks
clp->cl_sessions under clp->cl_lock to print each session's slot
counts.  free_client() tears down the same list without taking
cl_lock, and is the only unlocked mutator of cl_sessions.  A reader
can observe a client mid-teardown because get_nfsdfs_clp() pins the
nfs4_client but not its sessions: free_client() frees every session
before calling nfsd_client_rmdir(), so an in-flight seq_file reader
can follow a list_del()'d node whose ->next now holds LIST_POISON1
and take a general protection fault:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
        0xdead00000000014c
  CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 132488 Comm: cat
  RIP: 0010:client_info_show+0x2bf/0x3d0
  RAX: dead000000000100
  Call Trace:
   seq_read_iter+0x12a/0x4b0
   seq_read+0xf1/0x130
   vfs_read+0xbf/0x350
   ksys_read+0x6f/0xf0
   do_syscall_64+0x8b/0xcb0
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Detach cl_sessions onto a local reaplist under cl_lock, then free the
sessions after dropping the lock.  Removing entries from cl_sessions
under cl_lock matches unhash_session(), and the detach-then-reap shape
matches how __destroy_client() reaps cl_delegations.  The sessions
cannot be freed while cl_lock is held, since free_session() calls
nfsd4_del_conns(), which re-acquires it.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: drain join handlers before releasing module text

The code for a registered DLM handler must remain resident until its
last invocation finishes. dlm_unregister_net_handlers() only removes
dlm_join_handlers from the o2net registry. o2net_handler_get() takes a
kref on the wrapper, but that reference does not pin ocfs2_dlm text.
o2net_process_message() calls nh_func after dropping o2net_handler_lock.

With CONFIG_OCFS2_FS_O2CB=m, ocfs2_dlm can be loaded independently of
ocfs2_stack_o2cb while nodemanager continues handling messages from a
configured, heartbeating peer. If no dependent module or module reference
prevents normal unload, the following ordering is possible:

  Receive worker                       Module unload
  --------------                       -------------
  o2net_handler_get()
    take wrapper kref
    drop handler lock
  <preempted>
                                       dlm_exit()
                                         unregister handlers
                                       release DLM module text
  call saved nh_func
    in released module text

Use o2net_unregister_and_flush_handler_list() in the shared DLM
unregister helper. It first prevents new lookups, then waits for the
ordered o2net workqueue to drain, including a concurrent destruction of
that queue. The acquired invocation therefore finishes before dlm_exit()
returns and the loader releases the callback code. The same helper
covers partial registration and dlm_init() error unwind before module
memory is released.

Skip the drain when the private join-handler list is empty. Early
dlm_init() failures can reach this helper before any handler has been
published. Partial-registration failure also reaches it a second time
after the first call has already unregistered and drained the list.
Neither case needs to take o2net_wq_mutex or drain unrelated work.
The list is changed only by serialized module init/exit paths; a
nonempty list still uses the full unregister-and-flush helper.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: drain quorum work before removing the cluster

The configured cluster must remain available until an in-flight quorum
decision has finished using its fencing method.  o2quo_make_decision()
drops qs_lock before calling o2quo_fence_self(), which marks heartbeat
regions for unclean stop and then reads
o2nm_single_cluster->cl_fence_method.  Cluster removal clears the
singleton without waiting for this independent system-workqueue item.

When a failed-quorum decision overlaps removal of the heartbeat regions,
nodes and cluster through configfs, the worker can be preempted after
marking the regions and resume after the singleton has been cleared:

  Quorum worker                     Configfs removal
  select fence; drop qs_lock
  o2hb_stop_all_regions()
                                    remove regions; join heartbeat threads
                                    remove nodes; stop o2net
                                    clear singleton; release cluster
  read cl_fence_method

The resumed read dereferences NULL instead of applying the configured
fencing method. The heartbeat thread's dependency protects the local
node only until the thread exits, and draining o2net does not wait for
qs_work.

Add o2quo_flush_work() to drain pending or running quorum decisions
before clearing the singleton in o2nm_cluster_group_drop_item(). By
this point the heartbeat regions and nodes have been removed, so their
work publishers are stopped. The worker can finish while the cluster
and its configured fencing method remain available. It does not acquire
the configfs mutex held by the removal path.

Keep o2quo_exit() as the counterpart of o2quo_init() for module teardown
and initialization failure, and have it call the same drain helper.
Cluster removal uses only the explicitly named drain operation.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: pin owning modules for open debugfs files

The OCFS2 debugfs file operation tables do not set owner. The
full debugfs proxy obtains real_fops with fops_get() at open and
keeps it until final release. Without an owner, this does not acquire
a reference to the module containing the table and its callbacks.
Removing the debugfs entries does not drain retained open files.

An open connected_nodes file can therefore outlive ocfs2_nodemanager
and make full_proxy_release() read real_fops->release from freed
module memory. Heming also reproduced the issue with fs_state and
asked for the other OCFS2 debugfs operation tables to be checked.

Set owner to THIS_MODULE in all eleven explicit debugfs operation
tables: five in ocfs2_nodemanager, four in ocfs2_dlm, and two in

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: do not pass a NULL buf to is_oplock_break()

caller's bufs[]. Offload returns -1 with *num_mids = 0, so the

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race

Currently, init_cifs() calls cifs_proc_init() near the beginning of
the function, before INIT_LIST_HEAD, leading to a momentarily
uninitialized, but exposed, procfs. If a userspace process reads this

7.3.0-02212-g4df4d2a577db-dirty #6 PREEMPT(lazy)

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug

When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch
subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its
child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an
attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM
completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not
guaranteed numerically sorted).

I initially noticed this issue on a Dell XPS9720 when the system would
seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I
tried multiple kernel versions including v7.2.7 and v7.3-rc4 to see if
that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found
that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault
at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went
bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()` walk that I
ultimately ended up changing. To confirm this issue, I did an eBPF trace
of `bus_for_each_dev()`, `complete_rpm()`, and `complete()` while
unplugging in a variety of situations and found that an unplug from
domain 0 tries to `complete_rpm()` domain 1's switch, whose RPM
completion is not initialized and thus is holding a null wait-list
pointer, triggering the page fault.

Here are the key sections of that eBPF trace. Note that HEAD denotes the
completion's own wait-list HEAD:

```
RESCAN_ENTER domain=0

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=0-1 target_domain=0
         route=0x1 parent=0-0 unplugged=1
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=HEAD prev=HEAD

BUS_WALK domain=0 start=0-1 callback=complete_rpm
CALLBACK_ENTER rescan_domain=0 dev=1-0 parent=domain1 is_switch=1

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=1-0 target_domain=1
         route=0x0 parent=domain1 unplugged=0
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=0 prev=0

        complete+5
        complete_rpm+43
        bus_for_each_dev+133
        icm_free_unplugged_children+250
        icm_rescan_work+42
```

This patch gates the `complete()` on an additional condition - that the
Thunderbolt domain matches the domain of the device that was unplugged.

I only have a single system with multiple Thunderbolt domains - the Dell
XPS9720. I am consistently able to reproduce the Oops on that system.
Since running with this patch, I have not seen the Oops reoccur. I have
also tested it on a Thinkpad X1-Gen12, and that system boots and runs
well with it, but it only has a single Thunderbolt domain, so it does
not exercise the multi-domain failure case.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: cls_flower: avoid stale mask references after delete

Flower releases a mask reference when a filter is removed from the
classifier. The filter object can remain alive while dump, walk, or
hardware reoffload paths hold a reference to it. Those paths can then
dereference f->mask after the mask has already been released.

Keep the mask reference until the filter reference count reaches zero.
Release the mask synchronously from the final __fl_put() while the caller
still holds the tcf_proto reference, and leave the existing RCU work to
free the mask. This keeps the mask available to every reader that still
holds the filter.

The filter is still removed from the classifier indexes immediately.
Therefore, a deleted filter can temporarily retain an otherwise empty
mask; fl_delete() uses the handle IDR, rather than the mask list, to
determine whether the classifier has become empty.

Failed mask assignment can leave fnew->mask as an error or borrowed
pointer without an owned mask reference. Clear it before the common
failure path so the final put cannot release an unowned reference.

This fix does not add fields, snapshots, or per-filter memory.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Drivers: hv: vmbus: Bounds check the shared ring buffer indices

In a CoCo VM the host is untrusted. Since the VMBus ring buffer read and
write indices live in shared memory, the guest has to treat both as
potentially malicious.

hv_ringbuffer_write() copies into the ring at write_index with no bounds
checking, so the host can make the guest write packet data at any offset
up to 4 GiB past the start of the ring buffer. read_index matters too:
the available space derived from both indices is the only bound on how
much is copied, and an out-of-range index can make it far larger than
the ring.

The fix is to validate both indices before use and to use the validated
snapshot instead of re-accessing. For invalid indices,
hv_ringbuffer_write() logs and returns -EIO.

One re-read of write_index is left unchecked in this patch:
hv_get_ring_bufferindices() fetches it again for the prev_indices
trailer. The value is only returned to the host and is not used as an
offset or length for indexing. Since this is not a security issue, it is
addressed later in the series.

Open-coding the bytes available arithmetic keeps the fix free of
prerequisites; a later patch refactors it into a helper function.

items.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: deny access for an empty DACL instead of granting the request

smb_check_perm_dacl() returns the access mask it computes to the SMB2
CREATE handler, which uses it as the granted access for the open. For a
security descriptor whose DACL is present but contains no ACEs, the
function is supposed to deny access: an empty (non-NULL) DACL grants no
access to anyone except the object owner's implicit READ_CONTROL and
WRITE_DAC (MS-DTYP 2.4.5).

The empty-DACL branch only denies when both

  - the DACL has no trailing bytes (pdacl_size == sizeof(struct smb_acl)),
    and
  - the request contains bits beyond READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC.

In every other case it takes the shared "goto err_out" with rc still 0,
which returns success without modifying *pdaccess, so the caller grants
the full requested access. Three problems follow:

  - The READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC carve-out models the owner's implicit
    rights, but the check runs before is_owner is computed, so those
    rights are handed to *every* caller, not just the owner. For
    READ_CONTROL the SMB2 CREATE path does not fall back to
    inode_permission(), so any user can read the security descriptor of
    an object whose empty DACL is meant to deny them.

  - A request of exactly READ_CONTROL and/or WRITE_DAC is granted to any
    caller. WRITE_DAC lets the handle rewrite the DACL.

  - A DACL that declares zero ACEs but carries trailing bytes
    (pdacl_size > sizeof(struct smb_acl)) skips the deny entirely and is
    granted whatever was requested.

On shares where the NT ACL is the authoritative access control -- e.g.
"force user" shares, where every client maps to one POSIX identity so
POSIX cannot distinguish users -- this is an access-control bypass.

Compute is_owner before the empty-DACL branch and deny access from an
empty DACL unless the caller is the owner requesting no more than
READ_CONTROL / WRITE_DAC.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix OOB read and cross-share confusion in ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect()

ksmbd_validate_name_reconnect() indexes
ab_pathname[share->path_sz + 1] without checking that the path is
longer than share->path_sz + 1 (d_path() fills the buffer from the
end). A durable fp is not bound to its original share, so a client
can preserve a file from a short-path share and reconnect it on a
long-path share, making strcmp() read past the PATH_MAX buffer -
with a long enough share path this oopses the kernel, and on a
mapped page it also gives a byte-equality oracle on adjacent heap
(the reconnect succeeds exactly when the out-of-bounds string
equals the requested name). A same-share variant with the durable
fp at the share root reads 1 byte past the buffer
(strlen(ab_pathname) == share->path_sz).

Check before comparing: the path must be longer than share->path_sz,
it must start with share->path, and the next character must be '/'.
The share root itself is accepted only for an empty name.
